audit_items.reason: The functions cell_to_coset_evals and coset_evals_to_cell referenced in the checklist are specification-level (Python consensus-specs) functions. The Prysm implementation delegates blob/cell operations to the external c-kzg-4844 library (github.com/ethereum/c-kzg-4844/v2), which is a vendored dependency outside the bug bounty scope. The roundtrip property testing would need to be performed at the c-kzg-4844 library level, not in the Prysm codebase.

The _fft_field function referenced in the checklist is a specification-level (Python consensus-specs) function. The Prysm implementation delegates all FFT and polynomial operations to the external c-kzg-4844 library, which is a vendored dependency outside the bug bounty scope. The power-of-2 validation and FFT correctness would need to be audited at the c-kzg-4844 library level.

The fft_field and inverse FFT normalization referenced in the checklist are specification-level (Python consensus-specs) functions. The Prysm implementation delegates all FFT operations, including inverse FFT and normalization, to the external c-kzg-4844 library, which is a vendored dependency outside the bug bounty scope. The ifft(fft(p)) == p invariant would need to be verified at the c-kzg-4844 library level.

The ComputeCellsAndKZGProofs function is implemented in Prysm and is the trust boundary entry point for blob processing. While it delegates to c-kzg-4844, the Prysm wrapper is responsible for input validation and output verification.

validation_layers: Blob size is implicitly validated by fixed-size array type [BytesPerBlob]byte
Output array lengths are checked: len(ckzgCells) != len(ckzgProofs) triggers error
phase1_abstract_interpretation.trust_boundary: Function accepts blob from external callers (block proposers, validators)
potential_issues: No explicit BYTES_PER_BLOB validation before delegation to c-kzg-4844
No explicit check that output contains exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB elements
Relies on c-kzg-4844 library for all validation - no defense-in-depth

phase2_symbolic_execution.attacker_control: blob parameter can be influenced by block proposer/blob submitter
validation_sequence: Step 1: Blob copied to ckzg4844.Blob type (fixed size)
Step 4: Copy cells and proofs to result arrays
bypass_scenarios: If c-kzg-4844 library has a bug, no Prysm-level validation catches it
No verification that CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB (128) elements are returned

phase3_formal_verification.invariant: SG-020:INV-002: Input blob MUST be exactly BYTES_PER_BLOB, output MUST contain exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells and proofs

findings.title: Missing explicit CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB output cardinality check
findings.description: The function checks that len(cells) == len(proofs) but does not verify that the count equals CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB (128 for Fusaka/EIP-4844). If c-kzg-4844 returns an unexpected count, this goes undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit validation: if len(ckzgCells) != CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB { return error }

findings.title: No explicit BYTES_PER_BLOB input validation
findings.description: The function relies on the fixed-size array type [BytesPerBlob]byte to enforce blob size, but does not perform explicit runtime validation. While type safety provides strong guarantees, defense-in-depth would add an explicit check.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding runtime assertion: if len(blob) != BytesPerBlob { return error } for defense-in-depth

audit_items.reason: This checklist item references ommers validation for post-merge Osaka fork blocks. Prysm is a consensus-layer (beacon chain) client, not an execution-layer client. Ommers (uncles) are an execution-layer block concept. The UncleHash field found in the codebase is part of the execution payload interface but validation is performed by the execution engine (e.g., go-ethereum), not by Prysm. This is an EL/CL component mismatch.

This checklist item references P2P peer validation of ommers_hash for post-merge blocks. Prysm is a consensus-layer client that processes beacon blocks via P2P, not execution-layer blocks. The ommers_hash validation is an execution-layer responsibility performed by the execution engine. This is an EL/CL component mismatch.

This checklist item references execution engine validation of empty ommers invariant. While Prysm interacts with the execution engine via the Engine API, the actual validation of execution block structure (including ommers) is performed by the execution engine (e.g., go-ethereum), not by Prysm. This is an EL/CL component mismatch.

This checklist item references a trie root() function with deterministic, order-independent behavior. While Prysm uses trie data structures (found import of container/trie), the specific property appears to reference execution-layer state trie behavior. Prysm uses SSZ (Simple Serialize) for beacon state merkleization, not traditional Patricia/Merkle tries with key-value insertion order semantics. This appears to be an EL/CL component mismatch or specification mismatch.

This checklist item references a patricialize function with recursion termination guarantees. This function is specific to Patricia trie construction used in execution-layer state management. Prysm is a consensus-layer client that uses SSZ merkleization for beacon state, not Patricia tries. This is an EL/CL component mismatch.

This checklist item references a trie._data dictionary and trie_set operations with ghost entry prevention. This is specific to Python execution-specs implementation of Patricia tries. Prysm is a Go implementation using SSZ merkleization for beacon state. The trie operations referenced are execution-layer state trie operations, not consensus-layer beacon state operations. This is an EL/CL component mismatch and language/implementation mismatch.
